Alex — thanks for the clear asks and the appendix. Looping Karthik and Marissa for pricing/legal validation. Quick summary up front, full sample invoice and model attached (proposed-pricing-models.xlsx):

- Token floor behavior: annual committed floor (example: 120M tokens) settled quarterly. We invoice actual usage monthly; at quarter close we reconcile actual vs committed pro rata. If usage > committed in quarter, overage billing occurs at the overage rate in the SOW. If usage < committed, we apply a quarterly credit toward future invoices (not cash refund). This preserves predictable unit economics and gives you invoice smoothing.

- Handling spikes: we offer a 20% burst cushion on top of committed monthly run-rate for two months per quarter (no immediate overage). Spikes beyond the cushion bill as overage. Unused cushion capacity does not roll forward.

- Volume rebate ladder: retrospective rebate applied at year-end based on gross annual consumption against committed bands. Bands (illustrative):
  • Tier 1: 0–120M: standard rate (no rebate)
  • Tier 2: 120M–300M: 8% rebate on units within Tier 2
  • Tier 3: 300M–600M: 15% rebate for units in Tier 3
  • Tier 4: >600M: custom negotiated 
Rebate is calculated on billed spend and issued as invoice credit in the next billing cycle after annual reconciliation.

Attached: a worked example invoice (invoice-example-AtlasHealth.pdf) and the spreadsheet with line-item math. Karthik — confirm legal constraints and whether we should offer cash rebate for Tier 3 as an alternative to credit.

Next steps: I can host a 30-min pricing walkthrough + live spreadsheet review with your finance team on Wednesday 5/20 or Thursday 5/21. Which works best?

Thanks,

Alex / Rebecca — answers inline and a couple of alternative options attached:

1) Re: cross-SKU crediting — by default credits are applied at the account-level (single pool) to simplify finance ops. If AtlasHealth requires SKU-level chargeback we can implement a split reconciliation: credits allocated pro rata to SKU spend during reconciliation. That is operationally feasible but will need the initial mapping between product teams and SKUs and an extra line on monthly statements. (See tab 'SKU-split' in the spreadsheet.)

2) Burst cushion sizing — 20% is our standard conservative cushion based on median month-to-month variance we observe across enterprise customers. We can reduce to 10% for a higher commit; proposed switches:
  • Base commit 120M + 20% cushion (standard)
  • Or commit 150M + 10% cushion (reduced cushion in exchange for higher committed liquidity)
Both approaches keep the effective financial exposure similar; spreadsheet has Monte Carlo-ish scenarios (tab 'spike-sim').

3) Rebate application frequency — we can make rebates effective forward-looking quarterly once a new band is triggered (so if you cross Tier 2 in Q2 we apply pro-rated Tier 2 credit starting Q3). That requires a 60-day flagging window post-quarter to confirm band attainment and avoid churny reversals. Operationally we do not require year-end-only reconciliation.

Attachments: updated spreadsheet and policy note (see Drive link). Confirmed for Thursday 5/21 10:00am PT — I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Priya
